title: The Woman's Trick Against Her Husband
logline: A wife hides a live fish in a water jar, vanishes to a wedding for a week, and on her return uses the still living fish to convince the neighbours that her truthful husband is mad.
moral: Evidence that looks decisive can be wrong: the neighbours trusted the living fish and punished the man who told the truth.
tone: Dry satirical comedy that cools into a quiet, unjust ending. The fish is the innocent running gag; the husband earns real sympathy; no gloating at the end.

beats.summary: A man brings home a live fish on Friday and expects lunch after prayer.
A friend arrives with a wedding invitation.
She wants to go but the fish is not cooked.
She drops the live fish in the water jar and leaves.
She stays away for days; he waits beside the jar without knowing.
He searches house to house; nobody can help.
A full week passes: Friday again.
She returns and he confronts her in anger.
She answers by pulling the fish from the jar, still alive.
She tells the neighbours the opposite story.
He insists it was seven days ago.
The neighbours rule that a fish cannot live a week, so he must be lying.
They call him mad and lock him up, laughing.
He weeps, unable to convince anyone.
Evidence that looked decisive punished the one who told the truth.

cast.name: old woman neighbour
cast.look: Sharp eyed, the first to judge. Leads every staggered reaction.

cast.name: carpenter neighbour
cast.look: Big, slow, arms folded; counts on his fingers; does the grabbing.

cast.name: bean seller neighbour
cast.look: Eager know-all; speaks the verdict and laughs hardest.

scenes.summary: They believe the wife, call the husband mad, and take hold of him.

scenes.composition: The neighbours cross to stand round the wife at x 300..520; the husband alone at x 800 with empty floor between: a visible gap. The pointing arms make three parallel lines aimed at him.

actions.action: dabs one eye with the corner of her headscarf
actions.acting: head down, the hidden mouth corner turned up

actions.action: the bean seller twirls a finger beside his own temple
actions.acting: eyes rolled toward the others, mouth to one side

actions.action: a black scribble spiral pops over the husband head; HE IS MAD! above the group
actions.acting: the husband protests with arms out, shaking his head

actions.action: the carpenter and the bean seller stride over and each takes one of his arms; his feet leave the floor and pedal
actions.acting: he looks from one to the other, legs cycling in the air
actions.library: handLW/handRW to his elbows; walk phase with y lifted 20

scenes.summary: Bars slam shut on him. They laugh at his protests and leave. Alone, he weeps because nobody will believe him.

camera.notes: The wipe is the bars sliding across the panel. Medium (zoom 1.3) through the bars with the laughing group on the right outside them; after they leave at 139.6 a slow push to 1.9 on his face between two bars by 145.0.

scenes.composition: Cell on the left two thirds (x 60..640, floor y 900), bars in front; a small barred window high in the back wall at about (200, 380) with dusk sky. Husband at x 330 inside. Neighbours and wife outside at x 700..940. HA HA HA! over the group, not over him.

actions.action: iron bars slide across from the left and stop with a jolt in front of him
actions.acting: panel-only shake 3 units, the bars ring (1 unit vibration for 0.4 s); he stumbles back

actions.action: outside the bars the three neighbours laugh, each differently: bean seller bent double, carpenter head back, old woman behind her hand
actions.acting: shoulders shaking out of phase, lids 0.9

actions.action: grips two bars and shakes them, shouting; a small balloon with seven dots pops from him
actions.acting: two fist grip, talk wide, brow -0.6

actions.action: the group walks off to the right, still laughing; the wife goes last and glances back once, without a smile
actions.acting: her one honest look: flat mouth, 8 frames, then she turns away

actions.action: his hands slide down the bars and he sinks to his knees
actions.acting: slow (1.2 s), head following late
actions.library: person {kneel 0 to 1} + handLW/handRW on the bars

actions.action: his eyes fill; one tear runs down and drops
actions.acting: wet true, lid 0.4, small tremble, lower lip

actions.action: the little seven dot balloon drifts to the bars, sags and goes out dot by dot
actions.acting: he watches it go (gaze follows), then looks down

actions.action: forehead rests against a bar; a long blink
actions.acting: lid 1 for 0.5 s, breathing only

scenes.summary: The moral picture: the truthful man behind bars, and beside the cell the fish, the proof everybody trusted, swimming happily.

camera.notes: Slow pull-out from the husband (zoom 1.6) to a wide (zoom 1.05) by 151.0 that reveals the fish bowl on a stool outside the cell on the right, lit by a lamp. Then locked to the end.

scenes.composition: Two halves. Left: the cell with the husband sitting on the floor against the wall (x 300). Right: outside the bars, the bowl on a stool at x 800 (bowl rim y about 760) under a hanging lamp with a yellow halftone disc. A small scale icon hangs top centre at about (500, 300). Tags: PROOF on the fish side, TRUE on the bars. THE END in the upper third over the back wall, clear of his face.

actions.action: the pull-out begins; the husband slides from his knees to sit on the floor

actions.action: the bowl comes into frame on the right: the fish does a cheerful loop and a small splash
actions.acting: bright eye, quick tail; it has no idea

actions.action: a balance scale drops in top centre and tips the wrong way: the pan over the fish sinks, the pan over the man rises empty
actions.acting: tilt overshoots and settles at 12 degrees

actions.action: lifts his head and sees the fish through the bars
actions.acting: gaze to the fish, brows up in the middle, a slow blink

actions.action: arrow and tag PROOF pop on the fish bowl
actions.acting: pop with overshoot

actions.action: three ticks pop beside the PROOF tag one after another (one for each neighbour)
actions.acting: staggered 5 frames

actions.action: a second arrow draws from the PROOF tag across to the bars
actions.acting: draw on over 0.5 s

actions.action: the bars give one cold glint from top to bottom
actions.acting: travelling highlight 0.4 s

actions.action: a small tag TRUE pops on the bars beside the husband
actions.acting: he looks at the tag, then down

actions.action: the fish and the husband look at each other; the fish blows one bubble and turns its tail to him
actions.acting: his long blink; the bubble rises and pops at the rim

actions.action: THE END holds to 164.14; the fish keeps circling, the husband breathes, the lamp flickers
actions.acting: everything settles; one last fish blink at 163.0

ending.description: After the last word (160.76) the wide moral picture holds: the husband sitting behind bars on the left, the fish circling in its lamp-lit bowl on the right, the tilted scale above. THE END pops at 161.3 in the upper third and holds to 164.14 with a soft chime at 161.2. No smile, no gloating.

subtitles.ar: عاد رجل إلى بيته يوم الجمعة وفي يده سمكة،|وسلمها لزوجته وهو يظن أن الغداء سيكون جاهزًا بعد الصلاة.|طلب منها أن تطبخ السمكة ثم خرج لقضاء أعماله.
subtitles.en: On Friday a man brought home a fish,|asking his wife to cook it|while he went to his work and the congregational prayer.

subtitles.ar: لم تمض مدة طويلة حتى جاء صديق يدعو الزوجة إلى حفل زفاف في منزله.|رغبت في الذهاب، لكنها لم تكن قد أعدت الطعام،|ففكرت في أمر السمكة التي تركها زوجها.
subtitles.en: Soon a friend invited the wife to a wedding celebration.|She wanted to attend,|but the fish still had not been prepared.

subtitles.ar: بدلًا من طبخ السمكة، وضعتها حية في جرة مملوءة بالماء،|ثم خرجت إلى الحفل.|ولم تعد في المساء كما قد يتوقع زوجها، بل ظلت غائبة أيامًا متتابعة.
subtitles.en: Instead of cooking the fish, she placed it alive in a jar of water|and went to the wedding.|She did not return that evening.

subtitles.ar: انتظر الرجل زوجته وفتش عنها من بيت إلى بيت،|وسأل كل من ظن أنه يعرف مكانها.|لكن أحدًا لم يدله عليها،|ومرت الأيام حتى جاء يوم الجمعة التالي.
subtitles.en: The husband searched house after house for her|and asked everyone he could think of.|A whole week passed|before the next Friday arrived.

subtitles.ar: دخلت الزوجة بيتها أخيرًا،|فواجهها زوجها غاضبًا يسأل أين كانت طوال الأسبوع.|لم تجبه بقصة رحلتها،|بل أسرعت إلى الجرة وأخرجت منها السمكة، وكانت لا تزال حية.
subtitles.en: When she finally returned,|her husband angrily asked where she had been.|Instead of explaining,|she produced the fish from the jar, still alive.

subtitles.ar: جمعت المرأة الجيران لتدافع عن نفسها،|وروت لهم رواية تخالف ما قاله الرجل.|حاول الزوج أن يشرح أنه أحضر السمكة قبل سبعة أيام،|وأن زوجته اختفت منذ ذلك الوقت.
subtitles.en: The woman gathered the neighbors|and contradicted her husband’s account.|He insisted the fish had been brought home|seven days earlier.

subtitles.ar: نظر الجيران إلى السمكة الحية،|وقالوا إن بقاءها كل هذه المدة لا يمكن أن يكون صحيحًا.|صدقوا المرأة، واتهموا الرجل بفقدان عقله،|ثم احتجزوه وسخروا من احتجاجه.
subtitles.en: Seeing the living fish,|the neighbors refused to believe it could have survived a week.|They sided with the wife, called the husband mad,|and imprisoned him.

subtitles.ar: بكى الرجل لأنه عجز عن إقناعهم بما جرى.|وتنتهي الحكاية الساخرة من غير أن يُنصف،|تاركة مفارقة قاسية:|دليل ظنه الناس قاطعًا جعلهم يعاقبون صاحب الرواية الصادقة.
subtitles.en: The husband wept at being disbelieved.|The satirical tale ends without justice:|evidence the neighbors treated as decisive|led them to punish the truthful man.

new_assets.name: fish
new_assets.description: The planned side-view comic fish (shared with KD-007, KD-019, AN-111, AN-137), palette 0 blue-grey with yellow fins, 200 x 110 at s 1 (used at s 0.75). Fields used: flap (tail angle), eyes (open, wide, shut), gaze, lid, rot (hanging by the tail = rot 90 degrees), sq, plus a flat icon mode for balloons and clouds.
new_assets.implementation: Body as one K path (pointed oval), tail a triangle rotated about the tail root by flap, one dorsal and one belly fin, gill arc, round eye through eye2/EYE so the shared acting fields work; wrap with acting(). Swimming position from a keyed path (planned swimPath) with flap from speed.

new_assets.name: hangingJar (floor state, water fill)
new_assets.description: The planned clay jar with the oval cutaway window, standing on the floor without its rope, with a blue water fill, a slosh angle and room for a creature drawn inside the window.
new_assets.implementation: Add rope:false and fillCol to the planned hangingJar; clip to the window ellipse, fill water below a level line tilted by slosh (damped with swing()), then call an inside(ctx) callback for the fish; draw the rim and outline last.

new_assets.name: jailCell
new_assets.description: The planned bare cell (AN-114) with a barred window showing the sky and sliding front bars; here with an outside strip on the right for the laughing group and the fish bowl.
new_assets.implementation: bake() the wall (flat grey-blue with S.dots shading), floor band and window frame; window sky by skyCycle clipped to the opening with 3 bars; front bars as rounded rects with a black brush outline translated by (1 - shut) * -700 and drawn after the cast; return anchors {floor, window, barsX, outside}.

new_assets.name: weekDots
new_assets.description: The planned row of seven small discs (r 20, pitch 58) in panel space, n of them lit yellow with a star, the rest paper with a black outline; pop on each change. The running clock of the film (S1, S5, S7, S8, S11, S14).
new_assets.implementation: One function weekDots(ctx, x, y, {n, t, popAt:[...]}); each disc is a circle with settleTo scale on its pop time; also callable inside iconBalloon at 0.5 scale.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: The planned wordless picture balloon, single and three frame strip modes. Icons for this film: wedding (drum, two figures under an arch, heart), wife face with question mark, door with question mark, husband with fish, sun with TODAY, fish with tick, fish with X, dotted wife outline, weekDots.
new_assets.implementation: White rounded balloon with a black brush outline and a tail to a given point, pop scale via settleTo; content callbacks drawn clipped; strip mode divides the balloon into frames that pop on given times. Icons are Library figures at small scale or flat shapes.

new_assets.name: musicNotes
new_assets.description: The planned rising quaver glyphs (n 2 to 6) for the wedding invitation, the open door and the wife coming home humming.
new_assets.implementation: Seeded S paths from a point; each note is an ellipse head and a stem with a flag, rocking with K.noise and fading over 1.2 s.

new_assets.name: flush
new_assets.description: The planned anger flush: red dots climbing the face from the chin plus two steam puffs, for the husband at 84.72.
new_assets.implementation: A red S.dots patch clipped to the head circle with a rising clip line (0..1), and two dustBurst puffs at the headwear.

new_assets.name: person laugh / templeTap / handOver
new_assets.description: Planned shared helpers: the full laugh (mouth open, lid 0.9, lean back, shoulder shake) for the three neighbours at 137.46, the finger at the temple for the bean seller at 134.40, and passing the fish between two hands at 5.94.
new_assets.implementation: Small functions that return person pose fields from t (laugh: tip -0.1 and a 7 Hz shoulder offset; templeTap: handR near the temple circling 8 units; handOver: object eases from hand A to hand B in 0.25 s with a weight dip).

new_assets.name: cookPot, smallBowl (wide, water), scroll, balanceScale, worryScribble
new_assets.description: Small planned props and marks reused under their planned names: the cold cooking pot on a brazier, the wide water bowl for the fish, the invitation scroll, the tilted scale icon for the moral, and the scribble spiral over the husband at 135.28.
new_assets.implementation: Flat shapes with black brush outlines and dot shading, each one function with a few fields (pot: x, rock; bowl: fill, slosh, inside callback; scale: tilt; scribble: seeded spiral stroke with pop).

owner_questions: The Arabic says a male friend (صديق) invites the wife to a wedding at his house; default used: the friend is drawn as a cheerful neighbour woman at the door, which keeps the scene innocent.
The script says the neighbours imprisoned him (احتجزوه); default used: a plain barred cell with no chains or rough handling beyond being lifted by the arms.
Added running device not in the script: a row of seven day dots (weekDots) with the tags FRIDAY and FRIDAY AGAIN to make the week visible; default: keep.

Invented English lettering: FRESH!, COOK IT!, KNOCK KNOCK!, WEDDING!, PLOP!, WHERE WERE YOU?!, STILL ALIVE!, TODAY, 7 DAYS AGO!, IMPOSSIBLE!, HE IS MAD!, CLANG!, HA HA HA!, PROOF, TRUE; default: keep all (19 items).
The wife gives the viewer one wink at 46.14 and glances back without a smile at 139.60 (a hint of conscience that the script does not state); default: keep both.

SCRIPT: the English is a condensed translation; it omits Arabic details in P1 (he expects lunch ready after prayer), P2 (she thinks about the fish her husband left), P3 (she stayed away for days on end), P4 (nobody could direct him), P6 (his wife had been missing since then) and P7 (they mocked his protests). Both are kept verbatim.
implementation_notes: All cue times are word starts from planning/inputs/timeline.json on the final MP3 (161.14 s). The film runs 0 to 164.14 s.

People: Library person with costume presets (villager, villageWoman, maiden with a blue pal, oldWoman with hold:'stick', carpenter, beanSeller). Set LIFE.t = t for auto blinks; give every character a gaze target every frame (lookAt / gazePlan); explicit lid values need hand blinks.

Home: palaceHall {variant:'merchant'} baked once per u state; key u for the window (S5: 0.25 at 49.0, 0.5 at 50.6, 0.75 at 54.0, then 2.9 by 57.0; S7: continue to 6.25 by 76.0, then hold at 0.25 morning). Use the returned anchors for door, window, desk and stool; the coordinates in this plan are approximate and must be measured on the set.
Street: marketStreet strip w 2400 with camX tracking; neighbours stand in doorways (draw them before the door leaf) or behind the stall counter. Use townDoor open values keyed with settleTo.
The jar with the swimming fish must be visible in every home scene from 45.44 on (S5, S7, S8): the audience knows what the husband does not. Never let the husband look at it before 97.14.
weekDots sits in panel space (not world space) at the top of the picture; hide it in close shots where it would crowd a face (S9, S12).
Mask rule for the wife: smirk or sly eyes only while no other character is looking at her (36.88, 88.28, 108.90, 132.06); innocent or tearful otherwise.
Groups never move in unison: stagger(i) by 3 to 6 frames, old woman first. Speaker on one side, listeners on the other; balloons never over the speaker face.

Sound: only eight quiet effects, all in the listed pauses or after the last word (5.5 pop, 19.15 thud, 27.85 chime, 38.1 pop, 41.5 whoosh, 119.9 pop, 146.2 chime, 161.2 chime), master 0.6. Knocks, the plop, the bars and the laughter are visual only because the narration has no gap there.

Transitions: plain cuts except S6 to S7 (S.transition with caption DAYS PASSED..., camera key hidden at the card midpoint) and S13 to S14 (the bars slide across as the wipe; switch the set at the moment the bars cover the panel centre).
Shake is panel-only (translate inside the panel clip). Call the style finish last every frame. Lettering at least 44 px for headlines and 28 px for tags at 1280 x 720 scale; no dashes.
Subtitles: use the subtitles array (chunks marked with |), Arabic in Noto Naskh Arabic 700, English below in blue Bangers.
warnings: Narration is nearly continuous: only seven pauses of 0.6 s or more. Do not add effects on the knocks, plop, clang or laughter.
Six people in the home in S10 to S13: keep them at s 1.1 to 1.2 with the camera wide (zoom about 1.15) and check at phone size that the three neighbours read as three different people.
S12 close shot draws person heads at more than 2x: check line weights and that both eyes of each face are inside the panel.
fish, iconBalloon, weekDots, jailCell and the jar floor state are planned assets that do not exist in Library yet; build them in the story first.
The ending is deliberately unjust (the script says so). Do not add a rescue, a wink or a smile after 139.60.
